shots.note: Wide shot of the farm at first light, fog on the fields. Title appears.
Close-up: coffee mug steaming on a truck hood, boots lacing up.

sections.name: Verse 1
lyrics: Five in the morning, coffee's getting cold,
Diesel engines firing up, another day unfolds.
CLMS on the trucks, Ohio dirt on my boots,
Built a life from hard work and never forgot my roots.
Summer smells like fresh-cut grass, winter brings the snow,
A hundred people counting on which way I choose to go.
Three buildings and a farm, another deal on my mind,
Trying to build an empire without running out of time.

shots.note: CLMS trucks firing up in the yard before dawn, headlights on, breath in the cold air.
Close-up of the CLMS logo on a truck door.
Your boots in Ohio dirt, walking toward the crew.
Summer: crew mowing, fresh-cut stripes in the grass.
Winter: plow trucks pushing snow (last winter's footage works).
Morning huddle with the crew - the faces counting on you.
Driving past each of the three buildings.
You at the farm gate looking out over the land.
You at the desk late, phone in hand, plans spread out.

sections.name: Chorus
lyrics: I got a billion-dollar dream and a two-lane road,
A million things to carry and a heart that wants to go
Back to where Cheyenne's waiting, where my little boy sleeps,
Where the things that really matter aren't the things that money keeps.
I can buy another building, put my name upon the land,
But I can't buy back a sunset or the touch of her hand.
I'm chasing down forever on this little piece of earth,
And learning every day just what a minute's worth.

shots.note: CLMS truck on a two-lane country road at golden hour (drone or from a following car).
You driving, glancing at a photo of Cheyenne on your phone or visor.
Cheyenne waiting on the porch, dogs at her feet.
Your little boy asleep, shot from the doorway.
Your name/CLMS sign on one of the buildings.
Sunset over the farm.
Close-up: you and Cheyenne holding hands.
The dogs running across the field toward camera.

sections.name: Verse 2
lyrics: I've sat across from bankers, I've made some big-time plans,
Turned a little into something with these calloused working hands.
I know what it takes to win, I know what it takes to lose,
But the hardest thing I've ever done is knowing what to choose.
Sometimes I bring the weight of work right through our front door,
And give the ones I love the least when they deserve so much more.
Cheyenne's stood beside me through the sunshine and the rain,
And I'm learning being a better man means letting go of pain.

shots.note: You in a meeting or walking into a bank/office, sharper clothes.
Handshake across a table.
Close-up of your hands - dirt, scars, a wrench or shovel.
You alone in the parked truck, engine off, thinking.
Coming through the front door tired, still on the phone.
You set the phone face-down; Cheyenne looks up.
Rain on a window or a storm rolling over the fields.
Cheyenne hugging you in the kitchen.

sections.name: Chorus
lyrics: I got a billion-dollar dream and a two-lane road,
A million things to carry and a heart that wants to go
Back to where Cheyenne's waiting, where my little boy sleeps,
Where the things that really matter aren't the things that money keeps.
I can buy another building, put my name upon the land,
But I can't buy back a sunset or the touch of her hand.
I'm chasing down forever on this little piece of earth,
And learning every day just what a minute's worth.

shots.note: Dogs hanging out in the truck (parked or rolling slowly on the farm).
You, Cheyenne and the dogs walking the fence line.
You and Cheyenne on the porch at sunset.
Old photos from the early days: first truck, first jobs.
Drone over the properties.

sections.name: Verse 3
lyrics: I want my people proud to say they worked beside my name,
That I cared about their families more than fortune or the fame.
Want my son to know that strength ain't always standing tall,
Sometimes it's saying "I was wrong" and knowing when to fall.
I want to leave him something that a bank account can't hold,
A reason to be grateful and a heart that won't grow cold.
Teach him how to build a dream, but teach him how to stay,
And never let tomorrow steal the beauty of today.

shots.note: Company cookout - the crew with their families.
Shaking hands with an employee, both laughing.
Your son clomping around in your boots or hard hat.
Your son trips; you kneel and help him up.
Teaching your son something - riding the mower with you, using a tool.
Planting a tree together on the farm.
Your son playing with the dogs.

sections.name: Bridge
lyrics: If I make that billion dollars, if my name is known someday,
If I own a thousand acres and there's nothing left to chase,
I hope I'm sitting on that porch with Cheyenne by my side,
Watching our children living out the dreams we kept alive.
And when they ask me what I'm proud of, when my working days are through,
I won't talk about the money or the businesses I grew.
I'll say, "I loved your mama, and I tried to do things right,
And the greatest thing I ever built was waiting here each night."

shots.note: Two empty rocking chairs on the porch. Slow.
Slow motion: Cheyenne turning to camera in golden light.
Wedding / early relationship photos.
The house at night, porch light on, warm windows.
You kissing Cheyenne's forehead.

sections.name: Final Chorus
lyrics: I still got a billion-dollar dream and a two-lane road,
But I'm learning there's a difference between being rich and being home.
I still want to build an empire, still want to touch the sky,
But I don't want to miss this life while watching it go by.
So I'll keep on chasing mountains, keep my boots down in the dirt,
Keep on loving that Ohio land and giving all I'm worth.
And if I never make that billion, well, I hope I've learned
That a life that's full of love is more than any dollar earned.

shots.note: Big drone rise over the farm at sunrise.
Whole CLMS fleet lined up, crew waving.
Your boots and your son's little boots side by side in the dirt.
Hero shot: you, Cheyenne, your son and the dogs in the field.
Night bonfire, everyone laughing.
You and Cheyenne slow dancing in the barn or kitchen.

sections.name: Outro
lyrics: Three buildings and a farm, one woman holding my heart,
A little boy who calls me Dad, and dreams bigger than the stars.
Yeah, I'm still building something...
Just making sure I don't forget what it's all for.

shots.note: One of the buildings at dusk, lights coming on.
Cheyenne smiling at camera.
Your son running into your arms.
Stars over the farm. Hold, fade to black.
